video.title: Don't Swing AT the Ball on the Overhead

classification.reason: The coach provides executable cues and practice instructions, directing the player to find a comfortable hand throw spot and let the racket naturally slap the ball 15 to 20 degrees to the left of the hand throw path.

problem.title_as_question: Should you swing your hand directly at the ball on an overhead or serve?
problem.definition: Swinging or throwing the hand directly toward the intended target forces contact too late in the internal shoulder rotation, compromising wrist stability and fault tolerance.

symptoms.description: The hand throw vector and the ball trajectory show an angular offset of 10 to 30 degrees.
The wrist feels noticeably weaker at contact when trying to hit directly in the direction of the hand throw.
The player shanks or mishits the ball due to low fault tolerance near the extreme end of the motion.

causes.statement: Contacting the ball later in the internal shoulder rotation leaves the wrist structurally weaker and drastically reduces fault tolerance against shanks and mishits.
Attempting to hit straight toward where the hand is thrown forces the player to delay contact until a split second later in the shoulder internal rotation.
When the shoulder internally rotates, the natural slap of the ball occurs across the body, creating an inherent 10 to 30 degree offset from the hand's throw vector.

angles.summary: Shoulder internal rotation naturally directs the ball cross-body rather than straight along the hand throwing line.
Projecting the hand's throw vector onto the back fence shows it targeting the opposite service box while the ball travels to the target.
Both Ben Shelton and Andy Roddick throw their hand toward the same spot regardless of spin, letting internal rotation and forearm mechanics hit the ball cross-court.
Players wrongly believe they should swing the hand straight at the ball or intended shot target, which destroys disguise and wrist stability.

solutions.summary: Find a comfortable fixed spot (such as the middle of the opposite service box) to throw your hand toward instead of aiming the hand at the target.
solutions.external_goal: Throw hand toward the middle of the other service box.

solutions.summary: Throw your hand to the exact same spot while varying forearm rotation timing and amount (earlier, later, more, or less) to alter the shot target without giving away disguise.
solutions.external_goal: Keep hand throwing to the same spot while altering ball landing target.

solutions.summary: Feel yourself throwing the hand to a spot and allowing the racket to naturally slap the ball 15 to 20 degrees to the left of where you threw your hand.
solutions.external_goal: Allow the ball to shoot 15 to 20 degrees to the left of the hand throw target.
